payload.title: Wedding Destinations in March for Spring or Autumn Weddings
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s with AUD 150k or more to spend who have their eye on a March date (often for leave around the end of summer, or a year-ahead engagement) and are weighing an early-spring celebration in Europe against an autumn or late-summer wedding closer to home, and want to know honestly where March is mild, where it is wet, and what to ask before they commit.
payload.goal: Book a consultation with a Wedded Advisor (Speak with a Wedded Advisor).
payload.angle: March is a shoulder month almost everywhere a couple from Australia would consider: early, cool and sometimes changeable spring in the Mediterranean, mellow autumn in New Zealand, and the tail of the wet or cyclone season across much of the tropical Indo-Pacific. Most March lists sell sunshine. This page gives 10 unranked places we already plan and write about, split by what March actually is there, with March weather quoted only from an official source that names the station and period, the honest trade-off where March is cool, wet or in cyclone season, and two venue questions per place that turn the trade-off into a plan (wet-weather cover, seasonal opening, guest comfort).
must_include: Direct-answer intro (2 to 3 sentences): March is early spring in the northern hemisphere and autumn or late summer in the southern, and in parts of the tropics it falls in the wet or cyclone season; then exactly 4 one-sentence takeaways. Write fresh: do not reuse August sentences.

Short 'How to choose a March destination' section: mild versus wet, seasonal opening framed as a venue question, guests travelling from Australia, Easter as a question to check (no dates stated), plus one line on how the ten were chosen (only places we have a guide for; unranked).

Group 1 'Early spring in the northern hemisphere' (5 entries, unranked): Greek islands -> /destinations/europe/greece (timing link /destination-weddings/best-time-to-get-married-in-greece); Lake Como -> /destinations/europe/italy/lake-como-wedding (timing link /destination-weddings/best-time-to-get-married-in-italy); Amalfi Coast -> /destinations/europe/italy/amalfi-coast-wedding; French Riviera -> /destinations/europe/france; Portugal -> /destinations/europe/portugal.

Group 2 'Autumn and late summer in the southern hemisphere' (5 entries, unranked): New Zealand -> /destination-weddings/get-married-in-new-zealand; Mauritius -> /destination-weddings/mauritius-wedding; Seychelles -> /destination-weddings/getting-married-in-seychelles; Bali -> /destinations/asia/bali (timing link /destination-weddings/best-time-to-get-married-in-bali); Fiji -> /destinations/oceania/fiji. Bali, Fiji and Mauritius state the wet or cyclone season plainly, as the official source words it.

Same entry template for all 10: 'Why March' or 'The March trade-off' (one honest paragraph); 'March weather' quoted only from the official source naming station and period, linked at the claim; two venue questions; 'Our guide' link.
At-a-glance table: Destination | March conditions (as the source states, station named) | The trade-off. Values must match the entries.

FAQ (4 to 6 questions), e.g. Is March a good month for a destination wedding? Where is it warm in March? Is March cyclone season in Fiji? Is March autumn in New Zealand? Can we hold a symbolic ceremony abroad? Then close with one Wedded Advisor line from brand-facts 'Claims we can make' (e.g. 'One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments, works in your time zone and quotes in AUD.') plus the Speak with a Wedded Advisor CTA.
avoid: Prices, 'From AUD' figures or any cost comparison
'Best', 'top', rankings or numbering that implies order of merit (title already drops '10 Best')
Any temperature, rainfall or rain-day figure not quoted from the named official source with station and period
Calling March 'the best time' anywhere, or softening wet or cyclone season wording beyond what the source says
Research talk (e.g. 'we analysed', 'our research', SERP references)
Never link /destinations/latin-america-caribbean or /destinations/africa; no draft guides as entry links (Punta Cana is reserve only, with a LINK comment if used)
Stating Easter or school holiday dates, flight times, routes or visa rules
Copying or lightly rewording sentences from the August page; competitor wording or claims; em dashes; US spelling
AI images of any real destination

reserves.why_not_in: Early spring is cool or changeable (MeteoSwiss); weakest March case of the northern set and already in August. Swap for Amalfi Coast if the orchestrator wants a non-Italian entry.
Northern tropics, so it fits neither group; March sits in the wet season as NWS Honolulu describes it (to verify).
Guide is a draft (2026-11-25) and the Caribbean fits neither group; include only with a LINK comment if the orchestrator wants it.

mr_a.scope: Re-read the WMO World Weather Information Service pages from the August pack for March values: Milan cityId=603 (Lake Como), Naples cityId=604 (Amalfi Coast), Nice cityId=902 (French Riviera), Lisbon cityId=2 (Portugal), Port Louis cityId=1219 (Mauritius); HNMS Naxos station climatology (Greek islands). Reserve: Punta Cana cityId=596 and MeteoSwiss spring statement, fetched only if a reserve is swapped in.
mr_a.record: For each: mean max and min temperature, mean rainfall and rain days for March, normals period, reporting national service, URL, access date.

mr_b.scope: New Zealand (Earth Sciences NZ / NIWA autumn or March climate for a named station, e.g. Queenstown or Auckland); Fiji Meteorological Service (wet or cyclone season and March climate, named station); BMKG (Bali wet season statement); Seychelles Meteorological Authority (seasonal or monsoon statement for March); Smartraveller wet or cyclone season lines for Fiji, Indonesia, Mauritius and Seychelles. Reserve: NWS Honolulu wet season (Hawaii).
mr_b.record: Exact quoted wording for any season claim, station and period for any figure, URL, page date, access date.
